slide1_company_name.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_company_intro.value: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited (M&M), founded in 1945 and headquartered in Mumbai, is the flagship company of the Mahindra Group. It is India's #1 SUV manufacturer by revenue market share and the world's largest tractor manufacturer by volume (>41% domestic share), with major listed subsidiaries in financial services (MMFS) and IT consulting (Tech Mahindra).
slide1_company_intro.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_brand_portfolio.value: Flagship SUV brands include Scorpio-N, XUV700, Thar, Thar Roxx, Bolero, and XUV 3XO, alongside newly launched Born-Electric SUVs (BE 6e, XEV 9e). Farm Equipment brands include Mahindra, Swaraj, and Trakstar tractors.
slide1_brand_portfolio.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_business_model.value: Core industrial operations span Automotive (SUVs, LCVs, Last-Mile Electric 3Ws) and Farm Equipment (tractors and farm machinery), complemented by strategic listed holdings in Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services (52.2%) and Tech Mahindra (25.5%).
slide1_business_model.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_product_ecosystem.value: Integrated R&D at Mahindra Research Valley (Chennai), multi-plant manufacturing across Chakan, Nashik, Zaheerabad, Haridwar, and Mohali, and pan-India dealer and rural financing reach across 1,000+ districts.
slide1_product_ecosystem.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide1_strategic_approach.value: Capital allocation discipline focused on high-ROCE core SUV and tractor leadership, scaling Inglo electric SUV architecture, and maintaining strict balance sheet separation between industrial free cash flow and NBFC lending liabilities.
slide1_strategic_approach.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide2_company_name.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide2_executive_summary.value: M&M delivered strong consolidated performance in FY25 with Revenue from Operations rising 14.5% YoY to ₹1,59,211 Cr, Operating Profit (EBITDA) reaching ₹30,518 Cr (19.2% margin), and Net Profit (PAT) advancing 14.7% YoY to ₹14,073 Cr. Standalone core operations generated ₹15,150 Cr Auto EBITDA and ₹6,400 Cr Farm EBITDA.

slide2_thesis.value: Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) is essential for M&M because consolidated borrowings (₹1,29,025 Cr) largely belong to MMFS's retail lending book. Valuing Core Auto at 16.0x FY25 Standalone EBITDA (₹2,42,400 Cr) and Core Farm at 14.0x (₹89,600 Cr), adding MMFS and TechM stakes at a 20% HoldCo discount, and deducting ₹12,000 Cr Standalone Net Debt yields ₹3,64,196 Cr Equity Value or ₹2,929.98/share (vs ₹2,921.00 snapshot CMP).

slide2_key_highlights.value:
• FY25 Consolidated Revenue: ₹1,59,211 Cr (+14.5% YoY); Consolidated PAT: ₹14,073 Cr (EPS ₹113.22)
• Core Auto Standalone EBITDA: ₹15,150 Cr valued at 16.0x EV/EBITDA = ₹2,42,400 Cr
• Core Farm Standalone EBITDA: ₹6,400 Cr valued at 14.0x EV/EBITDA = ₹89,600 Cr
• Listed Associates (20% HoldCo Disc): MMFS (52.2%) = ₹14,616 Cr; Tech Mahindra (25.5%) = ₹29,580 Cr
• Less Standalone Net Debt: -₹12,000 Cr -> SOTP Equity Value ₹3,64,196 Cr (₹2,929.98 / share)

slide14_company_name.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide14_narrative.value: M&M's consolidated cash flow reflects the combination of industrial free cash flow generation and MMFS's NBFC lending operations. In FY25, consolidated Profit Before Tax reached ₹19,079 Cr with Cash from Operating Activities of ₹3,176 Cr (after NBFC loan book disbursements) and Investing outflows of -₹18,616 Cr. In our 5-year connected forecast (FY26E–FY30E), industrial CapEx is explicitly modeled at 5.2%–5.6% of revenue to fund SUV and EV capacity expansion.

slide16_company_name.source: Mahindra & Mahindra Limited FY25 Annual Report

slide16_current_ratio_narrative.value: Consolidated balance sheet ratios reflect combined industrial working capital and MMFS financial assets. Debtor days improved from 30 days in FY19 to 19 days in FY25, while Inventory days stayed tightly managed at 78 days in FY25.

slide16_quick_ratio_narrative.value: Cash Conversion Cycle improved to -21 days in FY25 (Debtor Days 19 + Inventory Days 78 - Payable Days 118), demonstrating strong vendor financing and negative working capital in core automotive assembly.
